note: Re-judged 2026-10-26 (independent judge, clean clone at c8584247bb) after 14d83a90bd changed applyConfig. Section 4.4.1: "Every SPD SHOULD have a nominal, final entry that matches anything that is otherwise unmatched, and discards it." The only change to applyConfig in 14d83a90bd is one statement: s.reloadPool(cfg.RemoteAccess) became s.table.virtualIP.reload(cfg.RemoteAccess, s.log) (virtual_ip.go). reload builds named eap.Pool descriptors and stores them in an atomic pointer; it touches no dataplane, installs and removes no SPD entry, and returns nothing, so it cannot refuse the apply. It still runs after installUnmatched, installIKEBypass, installSPDPolicies and setCookieThreshold, so the catch-all remains the first entry in on every apply. releaseSPD, shutdown, warnSPDLeft, installUnmatched and the other cited producers are unchanged. The virtual-IP work (a965d7c0d4) also substitutes the lease into the Child SA selector before the policy match (ts_narrow.go substituteVirtualIP); those Child SA policies are installed inside the engine window, above the catch-all, through the existing Child SA install path and its ledger. The three tagged units are unchanged: TestRFC4301DefaultFinalSPDEntryDiscards (with the leaf absent, the last entry in every direction and family is a wildcard discard), TestRFC4301FinalEntryIsUnderEveryZeSPDEntry (replays every recorded write through apply, a Child SA and shutdown, failing the moment any Ze entry is live without the discard catch-all), and TestRFC4301InboundClearPacketIsDiscardedByTheDefaultFinalEntry (real XFRM, a clear inbound packet matching no other entry is dropped). All three pass at HEAD under -race, the XFRM one executed rather than skipped; their discrimination records (parseUnmatched reverts, shutdown releaseSPD-first mutant) are current. Scope note carried from RFC4301-5.2-1: VPP holds no catch-all and the OSPFv3 RFC 4552 entries have none; those are the disclosed gap there and do not touch the SPD Ze's IKE engine builds, which these tests pin. Verdict stands.
